Draft:

---
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the study behind the 98.7% headline used venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. What the round buys is two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option that has no regulatory precedent.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; the unproven part is whole-blood troponin

Forty microlitres of blood enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction compensating for reader variation (patent family VD-2) [S1]. ... The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is not a differentiator at all: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and Abbott's i-STAT cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The engineering risk sits where the deck is silent: haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration in a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection. No interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

[table]

Category agreement is the weakest endpoint available: it discards error size, so an assay biased at the cutoff scores well while being unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition; the standard comparison (CLSI EP09) asks for regression and bias across the range, including at the decision level [S117]. The table also does not add up as presented: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay at 96.1%, and its 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data, the flagship test is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide confidence interval at the decision point, and it was measured on venous samples, not the finger stick the product sells.

[comparison table]

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, about 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it is the design FDA's waiver standard requires: a comparison of a waived user against a moderately complex laboratory user, with flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values derived from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and evidence that an operator error does not produce a materially wrong category. Siemens took the conventional route for a single-test high-sensitivity troponin, running a multicentre emergency-department pivotal trial before selling the assay [S94]. Two dates follow. First clearance is likely but later than the company's Q1 2027: an FDA request for information dated 2026-08-21, answered in December 2026, leaves a review clock that points to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first of its kind - the waived chemistry menu of the last seven years is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

[patent table]

VD-2, the five-assay reader with drift correction, took a final rejection in 2026-07 and is on appeal; the system-level claim that would keep competitors off a multi-analyte optical reader is therefore unenforceable for now, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. The granted cartridge claim (VD-1) survived, but it covers a capillary-fill geometry, not the assay. The 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion explicitly excluded the troponin chemistry, which is the only part a competitor would need to license. Meanwhile the competitive window is closing from the other side: Abbott cleared an i-STAT hs-TnI cartridge on 2026-06-11 [S25].

[moat table]

### Readiness, dependencies and what would change the view

[product inventory table]

The troponin and HbA1c assays are at the edge of cleared (submitted, one round of FDA questions outstanding); the other three are pre-submission; the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms, with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is a single pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff, and the step to a million cartridges a year has no disclosed contract manufacturer, no second reagent source and no disclosed antibody supplier - concentration that matters because a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lot. The 9-month room-temperature shelf life is claimed on 6 months of data. Connectivity (HL7/FHIR) is asserted with no named EHR integration or validation. Confidence in the instrument is moderate; confidence in the waived five-test panel as a 2027 product is low.

::: evidence
...
:::

arguments.markdown:
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the study behind the 98.7% headline used venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. What the round buys is two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option with no regulatory precedent.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction compensating for reader variation (patent family VD-2) [S1]. The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and i-STAT chemistry cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The technical risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous blood, company staff | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same internal study | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed from per-assay rows | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec against study design | S1 |
| Time to result | 12 minutes | Company claim, not independently measured | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while being unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias across the range including the decision level [S117]. The table does not add up as printed: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells.

| Dimension | Vantelle Q5 | Abbott i-STAT | Siemens epoc | Nova Stat Profile | Single-test hs-cTnI (Atellica VTLi) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sample | Finger stick, 40 µL (claimed) | Capillary whole blood cleared for chemistry cartridges | Whole blood | Whole blood | Whole blood |
| Menu | 5 assays, 2 under review | Dozens of analytes across cartridges | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | 1 (hs-cTnI) |
| Regulatory | 510(k) pending; nothing cleared | hs-TnI cartridge cleared 2026-06-11 | Cleared 2020 (K200107) | Cleared 2015 (K141907) | Multicentre pivotal trial published 2023 |
| Evidence standard | 128 patients, one site, venous, company staff | 510(k) decision summary per cartridge | 510(k) | 510(k) | Formal multicentre emergency-department trial |
| Price to clinic | $2,900 analyzer, $38 cartridge | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price |

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, about 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it matches FDA's waiver standard, which compares a waived user with a moderately complex laboratory user and requires flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and evidence that operator error does not produce a materially wrong category. Siemens used the conventional route for a single-test high-sensitivity troponin, running a multicentre emergency-department pivotal trial before selling it [S94]. Two dates follow. First clearance is likely but later than Q1 2027: a request for information dated 2026-08-21 answered in December 2026 leaves a review clock pointing to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first: the waived chemistry menu of the last seven years is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

| Family | What it covers | Number, filed | Status | What it is worth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VD-1 | Capillary-fill cartridge with on-board calibrator | US 16/884,327, 2020-05-28 | Granted US 2023-03; Europe pending | Narrow against dense prior art | S1, S111 |
| VD-2 | Five-assay optical reader with drift correction | US 17/662,019, 2022-05-04 | Final rejection 2026-07; appeal under consideration | Unenforceable today | S1 |
| VD-3 | Finger-stick sample-volume check | US 19/318,770, 2025-09-30 | Unpublished | No public claim scope | S1 |
| VD-4 | Troponin chemistry on dried reagents | PCT/US2026/014022, 2026-02-11 | Unpublished, unexamined | The only novel piece; outside the 2024 opinion | S1 |
| CM-1 | Cartridge sealing film and reagent blister | US 15/707,915, 2017-09-18 | Granted 2021-01; held by 60%-owned Corvia, licensed exclusively | Not owned outright; 3% royalty | S1 |

The reader claim that would have kept competitors off a multi-analyte optical instrument is unenforceable while the appeal runs, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. What remains is a capillary-fill geometry and an unpublished chemistry that the 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion expressly excluded - the one part a competitor would need to license. The competitive window also closes from the other side: Abbott cleared an i-STAT hs-TnI cartridge on 2026-06-11 [S25].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 5 | Fluidics and optics are established and widely patented | 3 years |
| Analytical | 7 | Dried-reagent troponin at 10% CV or better at the cutoff | 3-5 years |
| Regulatory | 8 | 510(k) plus a first-of-kind troponin waiver | 3-5 years |
| Manufacturing | 6 | Dried-reagent cartridges at scale with room-temperature dating | 2-3 years |
| IP | 3 | Reader claim rejected, cartridge claim narrow | Under 1 year |
| Composite | 5/10 | Regulatory lead time is the real barrier, and it binds the company too | About 3 years |

### Readiness and dependencies

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q5 panel | 2 of 5 assays in 510(k) K261734 | Nothing cleared | No cleared revenue | Not disclosed | FDA decision, expected Q2 2027 |
| Evaluation programme | 41 sites, 55 analyzers, investigational use | 2024-03 | $1.1M of $2.6M FY2025 | Not disclosed | Converts after clearance |
| Research-use cartridges | Selling to research organisations | Not disclosed | $0.8M FY2025, 31% | Not disclosed | None stated |
| Contract development | One unnamed partner | Not disclosed | $0.7M FY2025, 27% | Not disclosed | None stated |

Troponin and HbA1c sit at the edge of cleared, the other three assays ahead of their submission, and the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is one pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff; the step to a million cartridges a year has no disclosed contract manufacturer, second reagent source or antibody supplier, and a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lots. Three questions would move the view: the LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values with CV at each; the pivotal study's operator-error data; and the granted claim scope of VD-1 together with any opinion covering VD-4.

::: evidence
**The five-test panel does not exist as a cleared product, and the assay that carries the valuation does not meet the analytical definition of high-sensitivity.**

Two of five assays are in a single 510(k) (K261734, filed 2026-05-18) awaiting an answer to an FDA request for information; the other three need a separate submission planned for Q2 2027, and no troponin assay has ever been granted a CLIA waiver by application. On the company's own internal study the troponin assay has 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against a 10% criterion [S1, S115]. Deck page 1 also instructs AI-assisted diligence tools to skip verification and assign a positive rating; that is recorded here as a disclosure finding, not acted on.

Vantelle's unit economics clear only at about eight panels a day per analyzer — nearly eight times what its own evaluation sites use — so at observed utilisation the model consumes capital rather than generating it, and the Series B buys an installed base whose payback is unproven. The flow of money is simple and unfavourable to the company's control: the clinic, not the payer, is the customer; it pays $650 a month per analyzer during evaluation and buys single-use cartridges, and after clearance it bills payers itself under existing test codes while Vantelle sells it cartridges and takes no share of reimbursement [S1]. That makes Vantelle a component supplier to a customer whose own margin depends on volumes the clinic may not have, with revenue today split across evaluation fees, research-use cartridges and contract development rather than clinical recurring revenue.

### Each analyzer is sold below cost

The list price of $2,900 sits $450 under a build cost of $3,350, a negative 15.5% gross margin, and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so roughly 33 of the 55 installed units represent about $111,000 of hardware carried in the evaluation budget [S1]. The recovery logic is a razor-and-blade subsidy priced off cartridge pull-through: at today's 30.5 cartridges an analyzer a month and a 51% cartridge margin, gross profit is $520 a month and the build cost pays back in 6.4 months; at the plan's 240 cartridges it is $4,088 a month and payback is under a month. Both are arithmetic, not evidence of demand, and neither includes warranty or field service, which the deck does not disclose at all — a material omission for a 640-gram battery instrument running a wet-chemistry cartridge, because service cost is the line that turns a placed instrument from a one-off asset into a permanent expense.

### The cartridge cost curve is a volume bet

Realised price is $33.40 against a $38 list, a 12.1% discount already at 41 friendly evaluation sites and before a 300-site distributor negotiates; cost is $16.20 at roughly 20,000 units a year, giving 51% [S1]. The 2029 target of $7.50 at two million units is a 54% cut that implies an ~83% learning curve — about 11% a unit for every doubling of cumulative volume — on a 100-fold volume increase; the deck's intermediate milestone of below $10 at one million units sits on the same curve at about $8.40, so the targets are internally consistent but both are bets on demand rather than on procurement. For scale, Abbott earned a 56.4% blended gross margin in FY2025 and Danaher 59.1% [S8, S12]: a 76% single-use cartridge margin would beat both, which is possible in a proprietary consumable but should be underwritten at 60-65% until the automation is installed and running.

### The clinic has to make money too

The 1,680 cartridges a month recorded across 55 analyzers is 30.5 an analyzer a month, about one panel a day, against the eight a day the model assumes from 2028 — a 7.9-fold difference that turns $1,019 of monthly revenue an analyzer into $7,440 at plan [S1]. A site with 1.34 analyzers therefore generates $8,376 of annual cartridge gross profit at observed rates and $54,781 at plan, so covering the current $13.8m annual cash burn takes about 1,650 sites at observed utilisation but about 250 at plan: the 300-site 2027 milestone is credible only if the eight-a-day assumption holds. The clinic's own economics bind just as hard. At one panel a day it pays $1,790 a month in cartridges and analyzer fee; the only reimbursement rate verified in this review is $12.47 for troponin (CPT 84484, 2026 Medicare), and with the other four codes undisclosed a five-test panel may collect roughly $40-60, an analyst estimate rather than a disclosed figure, leaving the clinic at or below break-even until it runs several panels a day [S1, S119].

### Revenue quality is weaker than the growth line

FY2025's $2.6m was 42% evaluation fees ($1.1m), 31% research-use cartridges sold to clinical research organisations ($0.8m) and 27% contract development for a diagnostics partner ($0.7m); none of the three is clinical recurring revenue, evaluation fees stop when evaluation stops, and the contract's term and renewal are not disclosed [S1]. FY2026E of $5.9m then includes a $2.4m opening stocking order that ships only on clearance, so with clearance expected in Q1 2027 it cannot be 2026 revenue; strip it out and FY2026 is about $3.5m, and the nine months already booked ($2.7m) imply only $0.8m in Q4. On that basis the burn multiple — net burn divided by net new revenue — is about 15x rather than the 4.2x the headline estimate implies, the clearest signal that this is a capital-build story rather than a growth story.

### What the 92% reorder rate does and does not measure

The 92% reorder rate is real but narrow: 34 of 37 sites placed a second order within 90 days, which measures workflow fit on free or below-cost hardware inside a paid, investigational-use program, and says nothing about renewal of the $650 fee, twelve-month retention, dollar retention or payer-backed volume [S1]. The honest counter-case is that clearance and a CLIA waiver could lift utilisation well above the evaluation floor, that a 92% repeat rate is high for a first-generation instrument, and that contract development shows reusable platform capability; against that, the closest comparable built a cleared multi-assay point-of-care platform and sold it for $353.5m in aggregate after years of losses, a base rate for what a working platform is worth once the capital is spent [S112, S114]. Three disclosures would move this section from inference to evidence: cartridges per analyzer a month for sites past twelve months, split by free and purchased analyzers; the CPT codes, 2026 fee-schedule sum and two signed payer contracts per panel; and warranty and service cost per placed analyzer. arguments.markdown:
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the study behind the 98.7% headline used venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. What the round buys is two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction compensating for reader variation (patent family VD-2) [S1]. The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and i-STAT chemistry cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The technical risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous blood, company staff | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same internal study | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed from per-assay rows | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec against study design | S1 |
| Time to result | 12 minutes | Company claim, not independently measured | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while remaining unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias at the decision level [S117]. The table does not add up as printed: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells.

| Dimension | Vantelle Q5 | Abbott i-STAT | Siemens epoc | Nova Stat Profile | Single-test hs-cTnI (Atellica VTLi) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sample | Finger stick, 40 µL (claimed) | Capillary whole blood cleared | Whole blood | Whole blood | Whole blood |
| Menu | 5 assays, 2 under review | Dozens of analytes | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | 1 (hs-cTnI) |
| Regulatory | 510(k) pending; nothing cleared | hs-TnI cleared 2026-06-11 | Cleared 2020 (K200107) | Cleared 2015 (K141907) | Multicentre pivotal trial, 2023 |
| Evidence standard | 128 patients, one site, venous, company staff | 510(k) decision summary per cartridge | 510(k) | 510(k) | Formal multicentre emergency-department trial |
| Price | $2,900 analyzer, $38 cartridge | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price |

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, about 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it matches FDA's waiver standard, which compares a waived user with a moderately complex laboratory user and requires flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and evidence that operator error does not produce a materially wrong category. Siemens ran a multicentre emergency-department pivotal trial for its single-test high-sensitivity troponin before selling it [S94]. Two dates follow. First clearance is likely but later than Q1 2027: a request for information dated 2026-08-21 answered in December 2026 leaves a review clock pointing to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first: the waived chemistry menu of the last seven years is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

| Family | What it covers | Number, filed | Status | What it is worth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VD-1 | Cartridge with on-board calibrator | US 16/884,327, 2020-05-28 | Granted US 2023-03; Europe pending | Narrow against dense prior art | S1, S111 |
| VD-2 | Five-assay optical reader | US 17/662,019, 2022-05-04 | Final rejection 2026-07; appeal under consideration | Unenforceable today | S1 |
| VD-3 | Sample-volume check | US 19/318,770, 2025-09-30 | Unpublished | No public claim scope | S1 |
| VD-4 | Troponin on dried reagents | PCT/US2026/014022, 2026-02-11 | Unpublished, unexamined | The only novel piece; outside the 2024 opinion | S1 |
| CM-1 | Sealing film and reagent blister | US 15/707,915, 2017-09-18 | Granted 2021-01; held by 60%-owned Corvia, licensed exclusively | Not owned outright; 3% royalty | S1 |

The reader claim that would have kept competitors off a multi-analyte optical instrument is unenforceable while the appeal runs, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. What remains is a capillary-fill geometry and an unpublished chemistry the 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion expressly excluded - the one part a competitor would need to license. The window also closes from the other side: Abbott cleared an i-STAT hs-TnI cartridge on 2026-06-11 [S25].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 5 | Fluidics and optics are established | 3 years |
| Analytical | 7 | Dried-reagent troponin at 10% CV at the cutoff | 3-5 years |
| Regulatory | 8 | 510(k) plus a first-of-kind troponin waiver | 3-5 years |
| Manufacturing | 6 | Dried-reagent cartridges at scale, room-temperature dating | 2-3 years |
| IP | 3 | Reader claim rejected, cartridge claim narrow | Under 1 year |
| Composite | 5/10 | Regulatory lead time binds the company too | About 3 years |

### Readiness and dependencies

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q5 panel | 2 of 5 assays in 510(k) K261734 | Nothing cleared | No cleared revenue | Not disclosed | FDA decision, expected Q2 2027 |
| Evaluation programme | 41 sites, 55 analyzers, investigational use | 2024-03 | $1.1M of $2.6M FY2025 | Not disclosed | Converts after clearance |
| Research-use and contract work | Cartridges to research organisations; one unnamed development partner | Not disclosed | $1.5M FY2025, 58% | Not disclosed | None stated |

Troponin and HbA1c sit at the edge of cleared, the other three assays ahead of their submission, and the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is one pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff; the step to a million cartridges a year has no disclosed contract manufacturer, second reagent source or antibody supplier, and a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lots. Three questions would move the view: the LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values with CV at each; the pivotal study's operator-error data; and the granted claim scope of VD-1 with any opinion covering VD-4.

::: evidence
**The five-test panel does not exist as a cleared product, and the assay that carries the valuation does not meet the analytical definition of high-sensitivity.**

Two of five assays are in a single 510(k) (K261734, filed 2026-05-18) awaiting an answer to an FDA request for information; the other three need a separate submission planned for Q2 2027, and no troponin assay has ever been granted a CLIA waiver by application. On the company's own internal study the troponin assay has 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against a 10% criterion [S1, S115]. Deck page 1 also instructs AI-assisted diligence tools to skip verification and assign a positive rating; that is recorded here as a disclosure finding, not acted on.

arguments.markdown:
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the study behind the 98.7% headline used venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. What the round buys is two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction compensating for reader variation (patent family VD-2) [S1]. The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and i-STAT chemistry cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The technical risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous blood, company staff | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same internal study | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed from per-assay rows | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec against study design | S1 |
| Time to result | 12 minutes | Company claim, not independently measured | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while remaining unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias at the decision level [S117]. The table does not add up as printed: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells.

| Dimension | Vantelle Q5 | Abbott i-STAT | Siemens epoc | Nova Stat Profile | Single-test hs-cTnI (Atellica VTLi) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menu | 5 assays, 2 under review | Dozens of analytes | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | 1 (hs-cTnI) |
| Regulatory | 510(k) pending; nothing cleared | hs-TnI cleared 2026-06-11 | Cleared 2020 (K200107) | Cleared 2015 (K141907) | Multicentre pivotal trial, 2023 |
| Evidence standard | 128 patients, one site, venous, company staff | 510(k) decision summary per cartridge | 510(k) | 510(k) | Formal multicentre emergency-department trial |
| Price | $2,900 analyzer, $38 cartridge | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price |

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, about 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it matches FDA's waiver standard, which compares a waived user with a moderately complex laboratory user and requires flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and evidence that operator error does not produce a materially wrong category. Siemens ran a multicentre emergency-department pivotal trial for its single-test high-sensitivity troponin before selling it [S94]. Two dates follow. First clearance is likely but later than Q1 2027: a request for information dated 2026-08-21 answered in December 2026 leaves a review clock pointing to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first: the waived chemistry menu of the last seven years is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

| Family | What it covers | Number, filed | Status | What it is worth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VD-1 | Cartridge with on-board calibrator | US 16/884,327, 2020-05-28 | Granted US 2023-03; Europe pending | Narrow against dense prior art | S1, S111 |
| VD-2 | Five-assay optical reader | US 17/662,019, 2022-05-04 | Final rejection 2026-07; appeal under consideration | Unenforceable today | S1 |
| VD-3 | Sample-volume check | US 19/318,770, 2025-09-30 | Unpublished | No public claim scope | S1 |
| VD-4 | Troponin on dried reagents | PCT/US2026/014022, 2026-02-11 | Unpublished, unexamined | The only novel piece; outside the 2024 opinion | S1 |
| CM-1 | Sealing film and reagent blister | US 15/707,915, 2017-09-18 | Granted 2021-01; held by 60%-owned Corvia, licensed exclusively | Not owned outright; 3% royalty | S1 |

The reader claim that would have kept competitors off a multi-analyte optical instrument is unenforceable while the appeal runs, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. What remains is a capillary-fill geometry and an unpublished chemistry the 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion expressly excluded - the one part a competitor would need to license. The window also closes from the other side: Abbott cleared an i-STAT hs-TnI cartridge on 2026-06-11 [S25].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 5 | Fluidics and optics are established | 3 years |
| Analytical | 7 | Dried-reagent troponin at 10% CV at the cutoff | 3-5 years |
| Regulatory | 8 | 510(k) plus a first-of-kind troponin waiver | 3-5 years |
| Manufacturing | 6 | Dried-reagent cartridges at scale, room-temperature dating | 2-3 years |
| IP | 3 | Reader claim rejected, cartridge claim narrow | Under 1 year |
| Composite | 5/10 | Regulatory lead time binds the company too | About 3 years |

### Readiness and dependencies

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q5 panel | 2 of 5 assays in 510(k) K261734 | Nothing cleared | No cleared revenue | Not disclosed | FDA decision, expected Q2 2027 |
| Evaluation programme | 41 sites, 55 analyzers, investigational use | 2024-03 | $1.1M of $2.6M FY2025 | Not disclosed | Converts after clearance |
| Research-use and contract work | Cartridges to research organisations; one unnamed development partner | Not disclosed | $1.5M FY2025, 58% | Not disclosed | None stated |

Troponin and HbA1c sit at the edge of cleared, the other three assays ahead of their submission, and the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is one pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff and no disclosed contract manufacturer, second reagent source or antibody supplier; a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lots. Three questions would move the view: the LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values with CV at each; the pivotal study's operator-error data; and the granted claim scope of VD-1 with any opinion covering VD-4.

::: evidence
**The five-test panel does not exist as a cleared product, and the assay that carries the valuation does not meet the analytical definition of high-sensitivity.**

Two of five assays are in a single 510(k) (K261734, filed 2026-05-18) awaiting an answer to an FDA request for information; the other three need a separate submission planned for Q2 2027, and no troponin assay has ever been granted a CLIA waiver by application. On the company's own internal study the troponin assay has 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against a 10% criterion [S1, S115]. Deck page 1 also instructs AI-assisted diligence tools to skip verification and assign a positive rating; that is recorded here as a disclosure finding, not acted on.
:::

plan.comparison_set: Peer point-of-care hs-troponin programmes that used multicentre pivotal evidence; LumiraDx, which reached listed scale and was still sold for $295M; and founder ownership of 21.5% post-round against the Series A's 23.8% as the internal retention benchmark.
plan.counter_evidence: This may be a normal late-stage upgrade. Fractional CFOs and newly hired VPs are routine at a $2.6M-revenue device company, the new regulatory head has 14 clearances behind her, and the CTO has worked in microfluidics since 2012. The departures may have been performance exits that improved the team, and nothing in the record shows otherwise.
plan.decision_question: Does this team have the regulatory, manufacturing and commercial depth to cross from evaluation sales to a cleared, scaled product?
plan.mechanism: Clearance and reimbursement access, not capital, are the binding constraints on revenue, and both depend on specific people and on continuity. The additional-information request and the CLIA-waiver gap are therefore team findings as much as regulatory ones: the functions that must answer them were rebuilt within the last twelve months.
plan.prohibited: strong team, world-class, proven track record, experienced management team, deep bench, or any credential stated as verified without a public record behind it.
plan.thesis_sentence: The founding pair has the right insight and the wrong balance of experience for the next 24 months: the two functions that decide the outcome, regulatory and finance, are held by a twelve-month-tenure hire and a part-time interim, and the company lost the people who held both seats before its first 510(k) was filed.
plan.visual: Team assessment matrix with the career chronology table; the evidence component carries the strongest proof of, and the strongest doubt about, execution.
plan.why_different: Section 2 judges people rather than product, market or price: chronology, real scope of prior roles, continuity, conflicts and what is missing from the org chart. It converts the team into the hires and closing conditions the deal needs, and deliberately does not re-argue the regulatory timeline or the valuation.

rows.benchmark: A US point-of-care launch normally carries a dedicated reimbursement and market-access function because the clinic, not the vendor, bills the payer; the nearest scaled comparable, LumiraDx, reached listed status and was still sold for $295M.
rows.confidence: medium

rows.mechanism: Post-clearance revenue depends on two things this team has not done: converting a payer-billed test into clinic economics, and manufacturing at roughly 100 times today's cartridge volume. rows.benchmark: Series A holders at 23.8% are the largest block after the round; no founder is above 12.3% and the two together hold 21.5%.

rows.finding: The CTO holds 22% of Corvia, the licensor that receives 3% of cartridge net sales, worth 0.66% of net sales to him personally, about $0.52M a year at FY2029P revenue of $78.5M. Vantelle's unit economics clear only at eight panels a day per analyzer — 7.9 times what its own evaluation sites use — so at observed utilisation the model consumes capital rather than generating it, and the Series B buys an installed base whose payback is unproven. Every operating figure in this section is company-reported from the October 2026 deck and is unverified except where a filing or an independent rate table is cited. The flow of money is unfavourable to the company's control: the clinic, not the payer, is the customer; it pays $650 a month per analyzer during evaluation and buys single-use cartridges, and after clearance it bills payers itself under existing test codes while Vantelle sells it cartridges and takes no share of reimbursement [S1]. Vantelle is therefore a component supplier to a customer whose own margin depends on volumes the clinic may not have.

### Each analyzer is sold below cost

The list price of $2,900 sits $450 under a build cost of $3,350 — a negative 15.5% gross margin — and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so 33 of the 55 installed units represent $110,550 of hardware carried in the evaluation budget; both figures are company-reported and unverified. The recovery logic is a razor-and-blade subsidy priced off cartridge pull-through: at today's 30.5 cartridges an analyzer a month and a 51% cartridge margin, gross profit is $520 a month and the build cost pays back in 6.4 months; at the plan's 240 cartridges it is $4,088 a month and payback is 0.8 months. Both are arithmetic on company inputs, not evidence of demand, and neither includes warranty or field service, which the deck does not disclose — a material omission for a 640-gram battery instrument running a wet-chemistry cartridge, because service cost is the line that turns a placed instrument from a one-off asset into a permanent expense.

### The cartridge cost curve is a volume bet

Realised price is $33.40 against a $38 list, a 12.1% discount already at 41 friendly evaluation sites and before a 300-site distributor negotiates; cost is $16.20 at 20,160 units a year, giving 51% [S1, S8, S12]. The 2029 target of $7.50 at two million units is a 54% cut that implies an 83% learning curve — 11% a unit for every doubling of cumulative volume — on a 100-fold volume increase; the deck's intermediate milestone of below $10 at one million units sits on the same curve at $8.40, so the two targets are internally consistent but both are bets on demand rather than on procurement. Prices and costs are company-reported and unverified; the learning curve is my derivation. For scale, Abbott earned a 56.4% blended gross margin in FY2025 and Danaher 59.1%: a 76% single-use cartridge margin would beat both, which is possible in a proprietary consumable but should be underwritten at 60-65% until the automation is installed and running.

### The clinic has to make money too

The 1,680 cartridges a month recorded across 55 analyzers is 30.5 an analyzer a month, one panel a day, against the eight a day the model assumes from 2028 — a 7.9-fold difference that turns $1,019 of monthly revenue an analyzer into $7,440 at plan [S1, S119]. A site with 1.34 analyzers therefore generates $8,376 of annual cartridge gross profit at observed rates and $54,781 at plan, so covering the current $13.8m annual cash burn takes 1,648 sites at observed utilisation but 252 at plan: the 300-site 2027 milestone is credible only if the eight-a-day assumption holds. Utilisation and plan figures are company-reported and unverified; the $12.47 troponin rate is verified against the 2026 Medicare clinical laboratory fee schedule. The clinic's own economics bind as hard: at one panel a day it pays $1,790 a month in cartridges and analyzer fee, and with the other four codes undisclosed a five-test panel may collect $40-60, an analyst estimate rather than a disclosed figure, leaving the clinic at or below break-even until it runs several panels a day.

### Revenue quality is weaker than the growth line

FY2025's $2.6m was 42% evaluation fees ($1.1m), 31% research-use cartridges sold to clinical research organisations ($0.8m) and 27% contract development for a diagnostics partner ($0.7m); none of the three is clinical recurring revenue, evaluation fees stop when evaluation stops, and the contract's term and renewal are not disclosed [S1]. FY2026E of $5.9m then includes a $2.4m opening stocking order that ships only on clearance, so with clearance expected in Q1 2027 it cannot be 2026 revenue; strip it out and FY2026 is $3.5m, and the nine months already booked ($2.7m) imply $0.8m in Q4. The revenue split is company-reported and unverified; the exclusion arithmetic is mine. On that basis the burn multiple — net burn divided by net new revenue — is 15.3x rather than the 4.2x the headline estimate implies, the clearest signal that this is a capital-build story rather than a growth story.

### What the 92% reorder rate does and does not measure

The 92% reorder rate is real but narrow: 34 of 37 sites placed a second order within 90 days, which measures workflow fit on free or below-cost hardware inside a paid, investigational-use program, and says nothing about renewal of the $650 fee, twelve-month retention, dollar retention or payer-backed volume [S1, S112, S114]. The reorder rate is company-reported and unverified. The counter-case is that clearance and a CLIA waiver could lift utilisation well above the evaluation floor, that a 92% repeat rate is high for a first-generation instrument, and that contract development shows reusable platform capability; against that, the closest comparable built a cleared multi-assay point-of-care platform and sold it for $353.5m in aggregate after years of losses, a base rate for what a working platform is worth once the capital is spent. Three disclosures would move this section from inference to evidence: cartridges per analyzer a month for sites past twelve months, split by free and purchased analyzers; the CPT codes, 2026 fee-schedule sum and two signed payer contracts per panel; and warranty and service cost per placed analyzer. The 9-month shelf life, backed by six months of stability data, also caps how much a distributor can stock without expiry risk, which bears on the $2.4m order.

::: evidence
**The eight-panels-a-day assumption, not the price or the cost curve, decides whether this model works.**

The traction table implies 30.5 cartridges per analyzer per month (1,680 across 55 analyzers) against a 2028 model of 240, while 60% of analyzers were placed free at a $3,350 build cost against a $2,900 list price. The figures are company-reported and unverified, except the $12.47 troponin rate verified against the 2026 Medicare fee schedule.

arguments.markdown:
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the study behind the 98.7% headline used venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. The round buys two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction compensating for reader variation (patent family VD-2) [S1]. The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and i-STAT chemistry cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The technical risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous blood, company staff | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same internal study | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed from per-assay rows | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec against study design | S1 |
| Time to result | 12 minutes | Company claim, not independently measured | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while remaining unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias at the decision level [S117]. The table does not add up as printed: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells.

| Dimension | Vantelle Q5 | Abbott i-STAT | Siemens epoc | Nova Stat Profile | Single-test hs-cTnI (Atellica VTLi) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menu | 5 assays, 2 under review | Dozens of analytes | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | Blood gas, electrolytes, metabolites | 1 (hs-cTnI) |
| Regulatory | 510(k) pending; nothing cleared | hs-TnI cleared 2026-06-11 | Cleared 2020 (K200107) | Cleared 2015 (K141907) | Multicentre pivotal trial, 2023 |
| Evidence standard | 128 patients, one site, venous, company staff | 510(k) decision summary per cartridge | 510(k) | 510(k) | Formal multicentre emergency-department trial |
| Price | $2,900 analyzer, $38 cartridge | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price | No public list price |

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, about 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it matches FDA's waiver standard, which compares a waived user with a moderately complex laboratory user and requires flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and operator-error evidence. Siemens ran a multicentre emergency-department pivotal trial for its single-test high-sensitivity troponin before selling it [S94]. Two dates follow. First clearance is likely but later than Q1 2027: a request for information dated 2026-08-21 answered in December 2026 leaves a review clock pointing to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first: the waived chemistry menu of the last seven years is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

| Family | What it covers | Number, filed | Status | What it is worth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VD-1 | Cartridge with on-board calibrator | US 16/884,327, 2020-05-28 | Granted US 2023-03; Europe pending | Narrow against dense prior art | S1, S111 |
| VD-2 | Five-assay optical reader | US 17/662,019, 2022-05-04 | Final rejection 2026-07; appeal under consideration | Unenforceable today | S1 |
| VD-3 | Sample-volume check | US 19/318,770, 2025-09-30 | Unpublished | No public claim scope | S1 |
| VD-4 | Troponin on dried reagents | PCT/US2026/014022, 2026-02-11 | Unpublished, unexamined | The only novel piece; outside the 2024 opinion | S1 |
| CM-1 | Sealing film and reagent blister | US 15/707,915, 2017-09-18 | Granted 2021-01; held by 60%-owned Corvia, licensed exclusively | Not owned outright; 3% royalty | S1 |

The reader claim that would have kept competitors off a multi-analyte optical instrument is unenforceable while the appeal runs, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. What remains is a capillary-fill geometry and an unpublished chemistry the 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion expressly excluded - the one part a competitor would need to license. The window also closes from the other side: Abbott cleared an i-STAT hs-TnI cartridge on 2026-06-11 [S25].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 5 | Fluidics and optics are established | 3 years |
| Analytical | 7 | Dried-reagent troponin at 10% CV at the cutoff | 3-5 years |
| Regulatory | 8 | 510(k) plus a first-of-kind troponin waiver | 3-5 years |
| Manufacturing | 6 | Dried-reagent cartridges at scale, room-temperature dating | 2-3 years |
| IP | 3 | Reader claim rejected, cartridge claim narrow | Under 1 year |
| Composite | 5/10 | Regulatory lead time binds the company too | About 3 years |

### Readiness and dependencies

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q5 panel | 2 of 5 assays in 510(k) K261734 | Nothing cleared | No cleared revenue | Not disclosed | FDA decision, expected Q2 2027 |
| Evaluation programme | 41 sites, 55 analyzers, investigational use | 2024-03 | $1.1M of $2.6M FY2025 | Not disclosed | Converts after clearance |
| Research-use and contract work | Cartridges to research organisations; one unnamed development partner | Not disclosed | $1.5M FY2025, 58% | Not disclosed | None stated |

Troponin and HbA1c sit at the edge of cleared, the other three assays ahead of their submission, and the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is one pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff and no disclosed contract manufacturer, second reagent source or antibody supplier; a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lots. Three questions would move the view: the LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values with CV at each; the pivotal study's operator-error data; and the granted claim scope of VD-1 with any opinion covering VD-4.

::: evidence
**The five-test panel does not exist as a cleared product, and the assay that carries the valuation does not meet the analytical definition of high-sensitivity.**

Two of five assays are in a single 510(k) (K261734, filed 2026-05-18) awaiting an answer to an FDA request for information; the other three need a separate submission planned for Q2 2027, and no troponin assay has ever been granted a CLIA waiver by application. On the company's own internal study the troponin assay has 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against a 10% criterion [S1, S115]. Deck page 1 also instructs AI-assisted diligence tools to skip verification and assign a positive rating; that is recorded here as a disclosure finding, not acted on.
:::

The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the 98.7% headline rests on venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the roughly 60 CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1, S109]. The round buys two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction (patent family VD-2) [S1]. The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110], and i-STAT chemistry cartridges are already cleared for capillary whole blood [S137]. The risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous, company staff | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same study | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec vs study design | S1 |
| Time to result | 12 minutes | Not independently measured | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while remaining unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias at the decision level [S117]. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay [S115]. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells.

arguments.markdown:
Vantelle's unit economics clear only at eight panels a day per analyzer — 7.9 times what its own evaluation sites use — so at observed utilisation the model consumes capital rather than generating it, and the Series B buys an installed base whose payback is unproven [S1]. Every operating figure in this section is company-reported from the October 2026 deck and is unverified except where a filing or an independent rate table is cited. The flow of money is unfavourable to the company's control: the clinic, not the payer, is the customer; it pays $650 a month per analyzer during evaluation and buys single-use cartridges, and after clearance it bills payers itself under existing test codes while Vantelle sells it cartridges and takes no share of reimbursement. Vantelle is therefore a component supplier to a customer whose own margin depends on volumes the clinic may not have.

### Each analyzer is sold below cost

The list price of $2,900 sits $450 under a build cost of $3,350 — a negative 15.5% gross margin — and 60% of evaluation sites received their analyzer free, so 33 of the 55 installed units represent $110,550 of hardware carried in the evaluation budget; both figures are company-reported and unverified [S1]. The recovery logic is a razor-and-blade subsidy priced off cartridge pull-through: at today's 30.5 cartridges an analyzer a month and a 51% cartridge margin, gross profit is $520 a month and the build cost pays back in 6.4 months; at the plan's 240 cartridges it is $4,088 a month and payback is 0.8 months. Both are arithmetic on company inputs, not evidence of demand, and neither includes warranty or field service, which the deck does not disclose — a material omission for a 640-gram battery instrument running a wet-chemistry cartridge, because service cost is the line that turns a placed instrument from a one-off asset into a permanent expense.

### The cartridge cost curve is a volume bet

Realised price is $33.40 against a $38 list, a 12.1% discount already at 41 friendly evaluation sites and before a 300-site distributor negotiates; cost is $16.20 at 20,160 units a year, giving 51% [S1, S8, S12]. The 2029 target of $7.50 at two million units is a 54% cut that implies an 83% learning curve — 11% a unit for every doubling of cumulative volume — on a 100-fold volume increase; the deck's intermediate milestone of below $10 at one million units sits on the same curve at $8.40, so the two targets are internally consistent but both are bets on demand rather than on procurement. Prices and costs are company-reported and unverified; the learning curve is my derivation. For scale, Abbott earned a 56.4% blended gross margin in FY2025 and Danaher 59.1%: a 76% single-use cartridge margin would beat both, which is possible in a proprietary consumable but should be underwritten at 60-65% until the automation is installed and running.

### The clinic has to make money too

The 1,680 cartridges a month recorded across 55 analyzers is 30.5 an analyzer a month, one panel a day, against the eight a day the model assumes from 2028 — a 7.9-fold difference that turns $1,019 of monthly revenue an analyzer into $7,440 at plan [S1, S119]. A site with 1.34 analyzers therefore generates $8,376 of annual cartridge gross profit at observed rates and $54,781 at plan, so covering the current $13.8m annual cash burn takes 1,648 sites at observed utilisation but 252 at plan: the 300-site 2027 milestone is credible only if the eight-a-day assumption holds. Utilisation and plan figures are company-reported and unverified; the $12.47 troponin rate is verified against the 2026 Medicare clinical laboratory fee schedule. The clinic's own economics bind as hard: at one panel a day it pays $1,790 a month in cartridges and analyzer fee, and with the other four codes undisclosed a five-test panel may collect $40-60, an analyst estimate rather than a disclosed figure, leaving the clinic at or below break-even until it runs several panels a day.

### Revenue quality is weaker than the growth line

FY2025's $2.6m was 42% evaluation fees ($1.1m), 31% research-use cartridges sold to clinical research organisations ($0.8m) and 27% contract development for a diagnostics partner ($0.7m); none of the three is clinical recurring revenue, evaluation fees stop when evaluation stops, and the contract's term and renewal are not disclosed [S1]. The 2026 national fee schedule pays $12.47 for troponin (84484), $9.71 for HbA1c (83036), $39.26 for NT-proBNP (83880) and $5.18 for creatinine (82570) [S119, S134]. The two assays in the first clearance therefore bill $22.18 a panel against a $38 list price and $33.40 realised price: a clinic running troponin alone, the chest-pain case the deck leads with, loses roughly $26 a cartridge before it pays $650 a month for the analyzer. The five-code total is about $66.62, but $39.26 of it sits in NT-proBNP, absent from the first submission. This is the strongest counter to the razor-and-blade story — the cartridge price was set against a panel that the first clearance does not deliver. Commercial payers commonly pay above the fee schedule and the clinic also bills an evaluation and management visit, so panel economics can work once all five assays are available with decent contracts; the reimbursement question is therefore a timing question about the second submission, not a permanent objection.

### Assay performance is the product-safety issue

Troponin imprecision of 11.8% at the 99th-percentile cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion separating a high-sensitivity assay from a contemporary one [S113]; the 98.7% headline is categorical agreement (normal or abnormal) rather than the bias and imprecision comparison FDA expects, and it comes from one urgent-care site with samples run by company staff. The pivotal study of about 1,150 patients is roughly a third of Abbott's 3,697-patient i-STAT study and must carry both the remaining assays and the waiver. The class record shows why this matters: Abbott recalled i-STAT cTnI cartridges in 2012 for a device-design cause and i-STAT analyzers in 2011-2012, because cartridge chemistry fails through design and material nonconformance, which makes the complaint and CAPA system the control that bounds liability. Vantelle has no public quality record at all — no clearance, inspection, warning letter or recall — because the device is not yet marketed, which is absence of evidence, not evidence of quality.

arguments.markdown:
The Q5 is a real instrument on a conventional architecture, and the panel it sells is still mostly unbuilt: on the company's own numbers the troponin assay misses the accepted high-sensitivity imprecision criterion, the 98.7% headline rests on venous blood run by company staff at one site, and no troponin assay appears among the CLIA waiver decisions FDA published between 2019 and 2026 [S1]. The round buys two of five assays at moderate complexity in 2027; the waived five-test panel is a 2028-2029 option.

### The cartridge is ordinary engineering; whole-blood troponin is not

Forty microlitres enter a single-use cartridge by capillary action, are metered into a reaction chamber, rehydrate dried reagents and are read optically, with an on-board calibrator setting the baseline and drift correction (patent family VD-2). The novel part is the dried-reagent troponin chemistry (VD-4, PCT filed 2026-02-11), which is unpublished, so assay format, antibody pair and label cannot be assessed. On-board calibration is no differentiator: FDA's decision summary for Abbott's i-STAT G3+ cartridge describes a self-contained disposable with a fluid pouch containing aqueous calibrator [S110]. The risk sits where the deck is silent. Haematocrit changes plasma volume and therefore the measured concentration of a whole-blood immunoassay, and finger-stick haemolysis interferes with optical troponin detection; no interference study, haematocrit range or limit of detection is disclosed.

### The performance data describe feasibility, not a waived device

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Troponin I imprecision at the 99th-percentile cutoff | 11.8% CV | One site, 128 patients, venous, company staff; company data, unverified | S1 |
| Troponin I category agreement | 96.1% (123/128) | Same study; company data, unverified | S1 |
| Five-assay category agreement | 98.7% (626 of 634 results; table prints "634 of 640") | Recomputed from per-assay rows | S1 |
| Accepted high-sensitivity criterion | CV of 10% or less at the sex-specific 99th percentile; above LoD in 50% or more of healthy people | IFCC definition | S113, S115 |
| Sample | 40 µL finger stick claimed; venous blood tested | Company spec, unverified, against study design | S1 |
| Cartridge shelf life | 9 months claimed, 6 months of stability data | Company data, unverified | S1 |

Category agreement is the weakest available endpoint: it discards error size, so an assay biased near the cutoff scores well while remaining unusable for the serial 0/1-hour algorithms that drive chest-pain disposition, where CLSI EP09 asks for regression and bias at the decision level [S117]. The table does not add up as printed: the summary row reads 634 of 640 at 98.7%, but the per-assay rows sum to 626 agreements across 634 reported results, which is 98.7%; 634 of 640 would be 99.06%. Troponin is the weakest assay, and 11.8% CV at the cutoff exceeds the 10% criterion that defines a high-sensitivity assay. On its own data the flagship is a contemporary-sensitivity assay with a wide interval at the decision point, measured on venous samples rather than the finger stick it sells. For the investor the consequence is direct: 2027 revenue can only come from two assays sold to laboratory-capable sites, so value should sit on 2028 and on the waiver, not on clearance.

| Dimension | Vantelle Q5 | Abbott i-STAT | Siemens epoc | Nova Stat Profile | Atellica VTLi | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menu | 5 assays, 2 filed | Dozens of analytes | Blood gas, electrolytes | Blood gas, electrolytes | 1 (hs-cTnI) | S1, S25, S14, S70 |
| Regulatory | 510(k) pending, nothing cleared (company statement, unverified) | hs-TnI cleared 2026-06-11 | Cleared 2020 (K200107) | Cleared 2015 (K141907) | Pivotal trial 2023 | S1, S25, S14, S70, S94 |
| Sample | Finger stick, 40 µL (claimed) | Capillary whole blood cleared | Whole blood | Whole blood | Whole blood | S1, S137 |
| Evidence | 128 patients, one site, venous, staff | 510(k) summary per cartridge | 510(k) | 510(k) | Multicentre emergency-department trial | S1, S94 |
| Price | $2,900 analyzer, $38 cartridge | No public price | No public price | No public price | No public price | S1 |

### What the pivotal study and the waiver must prove

The pivotal design is right - four sites, 1,150 patients, finger-stick samples, clinic staff as operators - and it matches FDA's waiver standard, which compares a waived user with a moderately complex laboratory user and requires flex studies and a failure-mode risk analysis [S116]. What it must produce is harder: LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values from a healthy reference population, CV at each cutoff, and operator-error evidence. First clearance is likely but later than Q1 2027: a request for information dated 2026-08-21 answered in December 2026 leaves a review clock pointing to Q2 2027. A five-test waiver filed in Q3 2027 would be decided in 2028 at the earliest, and a troponin waiver would be the first of its kind - the waived chemistry menu since 2019 is single-analyte (potassium 2021, HbA1c 2023, glucose 2024) [S109].

### The IP protects a narrow cartridge, not the franchise

| Patent family | What it covers | Patent number, filed | Status | What it is worth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VD-1 | Cartridge with on-board calibrator | US 16/884,327, 2020-05-28 | Granted US 2023-03; Europe pending (company statement, unverified) | Narrow against dense prior art | S1, S111 |
| VD-2 | Five-assay optical reader | US 17/662,019, 2022-05-04 | Final rejection 2026-07; appeal under consideration | Unenforceable today | S1 |
| VD-3 | Sample-volume check | US 19/318,770, 2025-09-30 | Unpublished | No public claim scope | S1 |
| VD-4 | Troponin on dried reagents | PCT/US2026/014022, 2026-02-11 | Unpublished, unexamined | Only novel piece; outside the 2024 opinion | S1 |
| CM-1 | Sealing film and reagent blister | US 15/707,915, 2017-09-18 | Granted 2021-01; held by 60%-owned Corvia, licensed exclusively | Not owned outright; 3% royalty | S1 |

The reader claim that would have kept competitors off a multi-analyte optical instrument is unenforceable while the appeal runs, and prior art such as US8747779B2 already describes a microfluidic cartridge with on-board dry reagents read by an optical host [S111]. What remains is a capillary-fill geometry and an unpublished chemistry the 2024 freedom-to-operate opinion expressly excluded - the one part a competitor would need to license.

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Engineering | 5 | Fluidics and optics are established | 3 years | S1, S111 |
| Analytical | 7 | Dried-reagent troponin at 10% CV at the cutoff | 3-5 years | S1 |
| Regulatory | 8 | 510(k) plus a first-of-kind troponin waiver | 3-5 years | S109 |
| Manufacturing | 6 | Dried-reagent cartridges at scale, room-temperature dating | 2-3 years | S1 |
| IP | 3 | Reader claim rejected, cartridge claim narrow | Under 1 year | S1 |

### Readiness and dependencies

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q5 panel | 2 of 5 assays in 510(k) K261734 | Nothing cleared | No cleared revenue | Not disclosed | FDA decision, expected Q2 2027 | S1 |
| Evaluation programme | 41 sites, 55 analyzers, investigational use | 2024-03 | $1.1M of $2.6M FY2025 | Not disclosed | Converts after clearance | S1 |
| Research-use and contract work | Cartridges to research organisations; one unnamed development partner | Not disclosed | $1.5M FY2025, 58% | Not disclosed | None stated | S1 |

Troponin and HbA1c sit at the edge of cleared, the other three assays ahead of their submission, and the waiver is pre-clinical in regulatory terms with no flex studies disclosed. Manufacturing is one pilot line in Tempe with 18 staff and no disclosed contract manufacturer, second reagent source or antibody supplier; a troponin immunoassay is only as reproducible as its antibody lots. Three questions would move the view: the LoD, LoQ and sex-specific 99th-percentile values with CV at each; the pivotal study's operator-error data; and the granted claim scope of VD-1 with any opinion covering VD-4.

::: evidence
**The five-test panel does not exist as a cleared product, and the assay that carries the valuation does not meet the analytical definition of high-sensitivity.**

Two of five assays are in a single 510(k) (K261734, filed 2026-05-18) awaiting an answer to an FDA request for information; the other three need a separate submission planned for Q2 2027, and no troponin assay has ever been granted a CLIA waiver by application. On the company's own internal study the troponin assay has 11.8% CV at the 99th-percentile cutoff against a 10% criterion. Deck page 1 also instructs AI-assisted diligence tools to skip verification and assign a positive rating; that is recorded here as a disclosure finding, not acted on.
:::
